analysis:
This PR changes only docs/developer/build.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date and adds an interim-sizes note and edits the job-size table (patch excerpt truncated). The supplied base text covers lines 481-1157. It describes CI runner routing, job sizes, caching and the build process. It contains no executable code, no provider/coordinator wire changes, no key, attestation or authorization logic, and no prefix-cache storage changes, so assets A-001 to A-020 and threats T-041 and the TB-0xx boundaries are not affected by the change itself.

The documented change: production signs only 8x16 and 12x32 runner shapes, so lanes temporarily ask for 8x16, with test-cluster-gpu-2 asking for 12x32. The docs state that provider-plan.yml and scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py should be set back to measured sizes once 4x16 and 4x24 are signed. This is a CI sizing and availability matter. The route job keeps its Blacksmith fallback on any non-matching grant, per the base text at lines 549-557 and 685-696. The base text does not show the CI change weakening the cache gating (CI_ACTIONS_CACHE=off on Darkbloom hosts, lines 716-737) or the checkout .git sanitization.

I could not see the workflow files (provider-plan.yml, darkbloom-route.yml) or the truncated head table. Whether the real workflow edits are consistent with this documentation, and whether they preserve the exact-label grant check, is outside the supplied evidence. I raise no finding because docs-only drift is not a security regression. The integration pass should check that any accompanying workflow changes keep the exact-label match and the cache gating.
